k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Placed on the current street map (OpenStreetMap, S39): Pennington Avenue at Calhoun Street, taken as the site of Alexander Calhoun's house
k.say: Sketch legend B: Captain de Altenbockum's company of Lossberg's regiment (S36).
k.notes: Paraphrase of S21: the company was quartered at Calhoun's house (pp. 92-98, p. 148).

k.place: By Queen Street
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Placed on the current street map (OpenStreetMap, S39): Broad Street at Perry Street; how far down Queen Street is not stated
k.say: Paraphrase: the company retired by Queen Street after its captain was wounded (S21).
k.notes: Point is on Queen Street at the upper end of the town; how far it retired is not stated.

k.place: Old Barracks, where the River Road meets Front Street
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Marker coordinates (Historical Marker Database): Old Barracks, Barrack Street (S30)
k.say: Paraphrase: the jägers were quartered in the old barracks, with a post at Dickinson's house (S21).

k.place: Friends' Meeting House, Third (Hanover) Street
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Placed on the current street map (OpenStreetMap, S39): East Hanover Street at North Montgomery Street, the Friends Meeting House corner
k.say: Paraphrase: the dragoons were in the Friends' Meeting House (S21). The British light horse escaped (S20, note 10).
k.notes: Escape route not in the sources read.

k.place: King Street, by Rall's headquarters
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Marker coordinates (Historical Marker Database): "Headquarters of Colonel Johann Gottlieb Rall", 151 North Warren Street (S25)
k.say: Paraphrase: the artillerymen were in the Methodist Church and the English Church; the guns stood in King Street (S21).

k.place: King Street, near the bridge over Petty's Run
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Read from Wiederhold's sketch (S36), fitted to six points in the town centre (10-28 m misfit) and placed on the current street map. Letter O, on King Street just north of Rall's headquarters
k.say: Sketch legend O: Rall's cannons, "instantly dismounted" (S36).
k.notes: Paraphrase of S21: the two brass three-pounders were lost near the bridge over Petty's Run on King Street. They fired six rounds each (S33).

k.place: Marshy ground near the creek
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Read from Wiederhold's sketch (S36), fitted to six points in the town centre (10-28 m misfit) and placed on the current street map. Letter M, in the low ground by the creek
k.say: Sketch legend M: Lossberg's cannons "which sunk in the morass" (S36).
k.notes: Paraphrase of S21: the guns became stuck in marshy ground near the creek and were abandoned.

k.place: By the alley behind the English Church
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Read from Wiederhold's sketch (S36), fitted to six points in the town centre (10-28 m misfit) and placed on the current street map. Letter N, by the alley behind the English Church
k.say: Sketch legend N: Knyphausen's cannons (S36).
k.notes: The sketch places these guns in the town; Stryker has them later stalled near the creek (T45).

k.place: Near the creek
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Estimated by Claude from the place description; not measured. Low ground by the Assunpink east of Queen Street
k.say: Paraphrase: Lt. Fischer's two von Knyphausen guns were stalled near the creek; his horse was shot and the guns were later abandoned (S21).
k.notes: Still an estimate: the sketch shows these guns only at N, in the town (T60).

k.place: Richard Howell's house (cooper shop), Pennington Road
k.tb: Start: after the alarm on Christmas evening, when the post was reinforced (S21). End: TC01
k.cb: Pennington Avenue about 800 m from the head of the town. Distance scaled from Wiederhold's sketch (S36) against Calhoun's house; the sketch is not to scale outside the town
k.say: Sketch legend A: "picquet of 1 officer and 25 privet" (S36).
k.notes: Paraphrase of S21: a corporal and 15 men, reinforced to an officer, an NCO and 19 men. "About a mile northwest of Trenton" (S33). Strength: TC10.

k.act: Falling back on the supporting company
k.place: Toward Calhoun's house
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Placed on the current street map (OpenStreetMap, S39): Pennington Avenue at Calhoun Street, taken as the site of Alexander Calhoun's house
k.say: Paraphrase: the picket fell back across the fields toward Rall's quarters and was forced toward the von Altenbockum company (S21).

k.place: The Hermitage (Gen. Philemon Dickinson's house), River Road
k.tb: End: about three minutes after the upper picket was struck (S20; S21)
k.cb: Placed on the current street map (OpenStreetMap, S39): West State Street at Colonial Avenue. The Hermitage stood on what is now Colonial Avenue
k.say: "a commissioned officer and fifty men" and "a sergeant and fifteen men" are both given (S21). Sketch legend F: a detachment of 1 officer and 50 hunters (S36).
k.notes: Strength: TC03.

k.place: Along Front Street to the Queen Street bridge
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Marker coordinates (Historical Marker Database): Old Barracks, Barrack Street (S30)
k.say: Paraphrase: the jägers retreated along Front Street toward the Queen Street bridge; one was captured, the rest escaped and some fled to Bordentown (S21).
k.notes: Drawn as the stretch from the barracks to the bridge. Lt. von Grothausen escaped with fifty jägers (S20, note 10).

k.place: Fox Chase Tavern, Maidenhead (Brunswick) road
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Brunswick Avenue about 500 m from the head of the town. Distance scaled from Wiederhold's sketch (S36), letter D; the sketch is not to scale outside the town
k.say: Sketch legend D: picket of 1 captain, 1 officer and 75 men (S36).
k.notes: Paraphrase of S21: about 70 men; the principal picket. Hand's riflemen and the German Battalion "attacked the outpost there" (S33). What became of it is not in the sources read.

k.place: Queen Street bridge over the Assunpink
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Placed on the current street map (OpenStreetMap, S39): South Broad Street over the Assunpink Creek
k.say: Paraphrase: a sergeant and 18 men; its soldiers left the post without firing a shot (S21).
k.notes: S21 gives 18 men in one place and 19 in another.

k.place: Trenton Ferry road and landing
k.tb: Inferred from the sequence of events; no clock time in the sources read
k.cb: Estimated by Claude from the place description; not measured. Trenton Ferry landing below the town
k.say: Sketch legend E: detachment of 1 officer and 30 privates, which retired to Burlington (S36).
k.notes: Paraphrase of S21: one officer and 27 men; withdrew toward Bordentown. Still an estimate: the sketch is not to scale here.

k.place: Crosswicks drawbridge
k.tb: S21: news of the defeat reached it around 10 a.m.
k.cb: No position on record
k.say: Paraphrase: took no part and escaped capture; heard of the disaster around 10 a.m. (S21).
k.notes: Off the battle map; no coordinates.
